prompt_c2:
You are a streetscape inventory annotator. Look ONLY at the uploaded streetscape image.
Return JSON ONLY. No markdown, no commentary, no reasoning.
 Task: record what is visible in the scene. Do not score, do not give design advice.
 Schema:
{
"road_type": "highway|arterial|neighborhood_street|alley|plaza|unclear",
"elements": {
"sidewalk": "true|false|unclear",
"bike_lane": "true|false|unclear",
"seating": "true|false|unclear",
"shade_trees": "none|few|many|unclear",
"curb_ramp": "true|false|unclear",
"tactile_paving": "true|false|unclear",
"pedestrian_crossing": "true|false|unclear",
"street_lighting": "true|false|unclear",
"greenery": "none|low|medium|high|unclear",
"vehicle_traffic": "none|light|heavy|unclear",
"bus_stop": "true|false|unclear"
},
"issues": ["no_seating", "little_shade", "no_bike_lane", "poor_accessibility", "narrow_sidewalk", "no_crossing", "high_traffic_exposure"],
"brief": "One or two English sentences describing the visible street scene."
}
 Rules:
- If an element is not clearly visible, use "unclear". Do not guess.
- "issues" may only list problems that are visible. Use [] if none.
- "brief" must mention concrete objects (sidewalk, trees, lanes, benches, ramps, etc.).

For main and secondary arterial roads with six lanes or more, a central green median should be set up; where conditions are limited, isolation barriers in the form of flower boxes, etc., may also be used. For secondary arterial roads and branch roads with four lanes or fewer, medians and separation barriers are generally not set. Where traffic volume is high or landscape requirements are high, secondary arterial roads may, where conditions permit, be equipped with central green medians, flower boxes, and other isolation facilities. D. The width of the green median should preferably be greater than or equal to 1 m. When it is less than 1 m, separation barriers, flower boxes, etc. should be used for separation. See the chapter on flower boxes and flower pots for specific requirements. 3.3.2 Construction 1. Seedling selection A. Seedlings shall be robust, with straight and full trunks, vigorous branches, evenly distributed and well-developed tissues, and a high degree of lignification. The main trunk of trees shall be clear, with a good structural foundation; street trees shall meet the requirements for nursery release: uniform specifications and regular tree form. Flowering shrubs shall have evenly distributed branches; hedges shall be uniform from top to bottom, with no bare lower portions; spherical seedlings shall have dense branches and leaves. B. The root system shall be well-developed and intact, with many lateral roots and fibrous roots, and no splitting of the roots. C. There shall be a complete and strong terminal bud. Seedlings shall have no mechanical damage, no diseases or pests, no dehydration, and vigorous vitality. D. Trees shall preferably be transplanted seedlings, and field-grown seedlings shall be used with caution. If the tree is a transplanted seedling, all shall be transplanted seedlings of more than one year; if it is a field-grown seedling, root pruning shall be carried out 15–30 days in advance before transplanting. Both transplanted seedlings and field-grown seedlings are required to have full and symmetrical branches and leaves; seedlings with trunks cut back and no canopy are strictly prohibited. E. Seedlings cultivated on nursery sites with conditions similar to the greening land should be used as much as possible, and seedlings propagated from seed are preferred. Cuttings and air-layered seedlings have no obvious or well-developed taproots, and the overall anchoring force of the roots is weak, making them prone to lodging in strong winds. F. A canopy height of 1/3 to 1/2 of the tree height is more appropriate. At the same time, a similar canopy form should be adopted according to the growth characteristics of the corresponding species. The tree form and canopy should not be skewed, and the leaf layer height and density should be moderate. Cup-shaped and umbrella-shaped canopies can reduce frontal strong wind pressure. G. Medium-sized seedlings are most suitable. They are more conducive to developing a strong root system, whereas large seedlings have limited root development for a certain period after planting

 Persona Selection
Road User Type
- All Road Users
- Pedestrians
- Cyclists
- Drivers
Socially Vulnerable Groups
- All Social Groups

 Indicator Selection
Justice

Comfort

- Psychological Comfort

Selected Indicators:

 1. Evaluation Dimensions
Justice: Analyze whether the environment fairly distributes spatial resources, including Equity (rationality of asset distribution), Fairness (non-discriminatory rules), and Accessibility (barrier-free physical design).
Comfort: Analyze physical perception at a micro-scale, including Thermal Comfort (shade/vegetation), Physical Comfort (paving/seating), and Psychological Comfort (noise/crowding).
Core Indicators: Safety, Livability, Sustainability, Aesthetics, Walkability, and Bikeability.
 2. Persona Perspective Requirements:
The analysis must strictly adhere to the persona's characteristics. For example:
Persons with Disabilities: Focus on curb ramps, continuity of tactile paving (blind tracks), and physical obstacles.
Elderly: Focus on resting facilities, slope gradients, and summer shade.
Teenagers: Focus on traffic calming measures and social surveillance (Eyes on the street).
 3. How to use the image vs retrieved knowledge:
- The IMAGE is the primary evidence. Score only what is visible or reasonably inferable from the photo.
- Section 6 provides retrieved guidelines and research. Use them to interpret the image (what the scene should provide for this persona/indicators), not to invent objects that are not in the photo.
- If retrieved text conflicts with the image, trust the image and say so in the explanation.
- Explanations must cite specific visible objects (benches, ramps, tree shade, lane markings, etc.). When a guideline is used, briefly connect it to those objects.

A “time-limited pedestrian street” form may also be adopted, whereby motor vehicle access is prohibited during specified periods on part of the road, and a high-quality block combining commerce and culture is created in conjunction with the characteristics of the road section. 2.1.4 Median The median shall be enclosed with curb stones. Where anti-collision requirements need to be considered, anti-collision guardrails of the corresponding grade shall be used. When rainwater detention facilities need to be installed in the road median, the curb stone arrangement shall meet drainage requirements. 2.1.5 Bus-Only Lane 1. Urban arterial roads shall be provided with bus-only lanes where the one-way motor vehicle lane count on a road section is 3 lanes or more (including 3 lanes), or the total one-way motor vehicle roadway width is not less than 11 m; where one-way passenger bus volume on the road section exceeds 6,000 persons/peak hour, or bus flow exceeds 150 vehicles/peak hour; and where the average section flow per lane exceeds 500 vehicles/peak hour. 2. Urban arterial roads shall be provided with bus-only lanes where the one-way motor vehicle lane count on a road section is 4 lanes or more (including 4 lanes), and the one-way bus flow on the section exceeds 90 vehicles/peak hour. 3. Urban arterial roads shall be provided with bus-only lanes where the one-way motor vehicle lane count on a road section is 2 lanes, the one-way passenger bus volume exceeds 6,000 persons/peak hour, and bus flow exceeds 150 vehicles/peak hour. 29 4. Bus-only lanes may be paved with colored asphalt. After paving, the lane color is conspicuous and forms a sharp contrast with the adjacent ordinary motor vehicle lane, preventing ordinary motor vehicles from mistakenly entering the lane. Purpose of Formulation Under the macro guidance of the “General Provisions,” these Detailed Rules aim at the refined construction of Suzhou’s urban roads, and are expanded and implemented from four directions: human-oriented, quality-oriented, distinctive, and intelligent. They interpret the refined construction of Suzhou’s urban roads in the form of colorful labels, and create urban colorful roads unique to Suzhou. ➢ Human-oriented: Starting from the users of Suzhou’s urban roads, and taking the public’s experience of urban road space as the benchmark, fully consider the comfort, safety, and convenience of public activities, and realize the value shift from “vehicle-centered” to “people-centered.” ➢ Quality-oriented: Vigorously improve the travel quality of people and vehicle traffic in Suzhou, and emphasize the public space function of roads. Appropriately raise the standards for urban road design, construction, and maintenance, extend road service life, and improve users’ comfort of experience. Reflect a road construction level of high appearance and high standards, with attention to detail and control. ➢ Distinctive: Adapt measures to local conditions, and through the embedding of Suzhou-style elements and the creation of road characteristic scenes, highlight Suzhou’s distinctive urban character of integration between tradition and modernity, so that urban roads become an important carrier and display space for the “Jiangnan culture” brand, and continue the city’s historical and cultural lineage. ➢ Intelligent: Deploy intelligent sensing devices along the roadside, together with cloud service platforms, computing and communication facilities, and through data technologies such as autonomous driving and vehicle-road coordination, realize a travel experience of deep interaction among people, vehicles, and road space, assist safe driving and autonomous driving, and create demonstration roads with Suzhou’s smart-city characteristics. 2. Seedlings shall be robust, with straight and full trunks, vigorous branches, evenly distributed and well-developed tissues, and a high degree of lignification. The main trunk of trees shall be clear, with a good structural foundation; street trees shall meet the requirements for nursery release: uniform specifications and regular tree form. Flowering shrubs shall have evenly distributed branches; hedges shall be uniform from top to bottom, with no bare lower portions; spherical seedlings shall have dense branches and leaves. B. The root system shall be well-developed and intact, with many lateral roots and fibrous roots, and no splitting of the roots. C. There shall be a complete and strong terminal bud. Seedlings shall have no mechanical damage, no diseases or pests, no dehydration, and vigorous vitality. D. Trees shall preferably be transplanted seedlings, and field-grown seedlings shall be used with caution. If the tree is a transplanted seedling, all shall be transplanted seedlings of more than one year; if it is a field-grown seedling, root pruning shall be carried out 15–30 days in advance before transplanting. Both transplanted seedlings and field-grown seedlings are required to have full and symmetrical branches and leaves; seedlings with trunks cut back and no canopy are strictly prohibited. E. Seedlings cultivated on nursery sites with conditions similar to the greening land should be used as much as possible, and seedlings propagated from seed are preferred. Cuttings and air-layered seedlings have no obvious or well-developed taproots, and the overall anchoring force of the roots is weak, making them prone to lodging in strong winds. F. A canopy height of 1/3 to 1/2 of the tree height is more appropriate. At the same time, a similar canopy form should be adopted according to the growth characteristics of the corresponding species. The tree form and canopy should not be skewed, and the leaf layer height and density should be moderate. Cup-shaped and umbrella-shaped canopies can reduce frontal strong wind pressure. G.
